text.p: The targets of bomb attacks launched by IRA guerrillas in mainland Britain over the past quarter-century range from prime ministers to ordinary citizens.
Two suspected IRA blasts in northern England caused damage to railway lines and signalling equipment on Wednesday. The guerrilla group ended a 17-month ceasefire in February 1996.
Here is a chronology of major attacks by the IRA carried out in mainland Britain:
Feb 22 - A bomb at an army officers' mess at Aldershot, near London, kills seven people and injures 19.
Feb 4 - A coach carrying soldiers and families from Manchester is blown up, killing 12 people and injuring 14.
Oct 5 - Two tavern bars are bombed in Guildford, near London, killing five people and injuring 35.
Nov 7 - A bomb explodes in a pub in Woolwich, southeast London. Two people die and 27 are injured.
Nov 21 - Two Birmingham pubs are bombed. Twenty-one people die and 162 are injured.
Jul 20 - Two bomb attacks are aimed at soldiers in London parks, one in Hyde Park and one in Regent's Park. Eleven people are killed and 50 injured.
Dec 17 - Six people are killed by a bomb outside Harrods store in London.
Oct 12 - Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher narrowly escapes injury in bomb attack at Grand Hotel, Brighton, during a party Conference. Five people are killed and 30 injured.
Sept 22 - A bomb explodes at the Royal Marines School of Music barracks in Deal, southeast England, killing 11 people and injuring 22.
July 30 - Conservative MP Ian Gow killed by a car bomb at his home in East Sussex, southeast England.
Feb 7 - A mortar bomb attack is launched on No.10 Downing Street, the official residence of Prime Minister John Major
Feb 18 - A bomb explodes at London's Victoria station, killing one man and injuring at least 38 people.
Apr 10 - A huge car bomb explodes near the Baltic Exchange international shipping market in the heart of London's financial district. Three people were killed and 91 injured.
Oct 12 - The eighth bomb in a week planted by the IRA explodes in the Sussex Arms pub in Covent Garden area of London. At least five people are injured and one man later dies.
Mar 20 - Two bombs, hidden in litter bins in a shopping centre in Warrington, kill a three-year-old boy and injure 56 bystanders. A second boy, aged 12, dies five days later.
Apr 24 - A bomb explodes in Bishopsgate, central London. One person is killed and over 40 are injured.
Sept 1, 1994 - Feb 8, 1996 - The IRA observes a 17-month ceasefire, matched in October 1994 by a cessation of military operations by Protestant Loyalist foes in Northern Ireland.
Feb 9 - IRA declares ceasefire is over. Minutes later, a huge bomb rocks the Docklands business district of east London, killing two people and injuring 100.
Feb 18 - A bomb being carried by IRA volunteer explodes on a London bus, killing one person and injuring eight.
Mar 9 - A bomb explodes near West Brompton underground station in London. There are no injuries.
Jun 15 - Bomb in a van explodes in a shopping centre in Manchester injuring over 200 people.
March 26 - Two suspected IRA bombs damage railway tracks and signalling equipment in Wilmslow in an apparent bid to cause disruption ahead of the May 1 election.
